docRequirement: agent-sdk/subagents.md:190 — "By default, subagents can spawn subagents of their own, up to three layers below the main conversation. To change the limit, set `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` to the number of subagent layers you want below your main conversation, or `1` to turn nesting off". env-vars.md:280 fixes the reader's semantics: "Number of subagent layers allowed below the main conversation (default: 3) ... Accepts a positive whole number in plain digits; anything else is ignored, so the limit can be adjusted but not removed." sub-agents.md:862 adds the at-limit rule: "At the depth limit, Claude Code withholds the `Agent` tool from every subagent except a fork ... A fork at the limit keeps `Agent` in its inherited tool list, but the tool returns an error instead of spawning." So we are bound to (a) a default ceiling of three subagent layers, and (b) an env-var override honouring `1` as "nesting off".
current: The ceiling is 1 and there is no override anywhere. `packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:110` — `export const DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH = 1`, with a comment requiring lockstep with the host default. `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-manifest.ts:107` — `depth: 1` inside `DEFAULT_PI_ORCHESTRATOR_CONFIG`. The refusal is `spawner.ts:518-519`: `if (depth > (cfg.maxDepth ?? DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH)) return failure(args.agentDef.name, ` + "`Subagent depth limit exceeded (${cfg.maxDepth ?? DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH})`)" — child depth is `(args.depth ?? 0) + 1` (:515), so any grandchild is refused. The spawner reads `maxDepth` only from `packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1279` (`maxDepth: config.orchestrator?.depth`), whose `config.orchestrator` is the normalized execution manifest (`index.ts:2766`, `harness-manifest.ts:251` `depth: positiveInteger(value.depth, 'orchestrator.depth')`). The one production builder of that seed — `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:4148-4163` — populates `contextSeed`, `sessionDepth`, `sessionIsFork`, `forkSubagent` and `tierModelMap` and never `depth`, so `normalizePiOrchestratorConfig` fills 1 on every real session; only `packages/pi-agent-server/scripts/smoke-orchestrator.ts:241` ever passes a higher value. A fourth default sits at `SessionManager.ts:4932` (`maxDepth: parentBudgets?.maxDepth ?? 1`) on the plugin-hook agent-spawn path. No env reader exists: `grep -ran "NESSY_[A-Z_]*DEPTH|MAX_SUBAGENT|SUBAGENT_SPAWN" packages apps scripts` returns nothing, and `grep -ran SPAWN_DEPTH` over the whole repo (no --include, so NUL-byte files cannot hide) returns only prose under `docs/`. The behaviour is pinned by tests: `packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.test.ts:532` asserts both defaults are 1 and `:537-546` asserts a grandchild errors with 'depth limit' while the child succeeds (positive control at `:549-553`, which raises `maxDepth` to 2 and the same grandchild then succeeds). `packages/pi-agent-server/README.md:31` and `:47` document `depth` default `1`, "Default is ONE level of delegation".
divergence: Two deltas, both on the same knob. (1) VALUE: our default ceiling is 1 where the page says 3 — i.e. we ship Claude's documented "turn nesting off" setting as the unconditional product behaviour. (2) NO OVERRIDE PATH: `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` has no `NESSY_`-prefixed counterpart, and the `orchestrator.depth` knob that would carry it (`pi-agent-server/README.md:47`) is never populated by host code, so the ceiling is fixed at 1 rather than merely defaulted to 1. The key names and the wire shape are right — `PiOrchestratorConfig.depth` and `budgets.maxDepth` already exist, are validated and are honoured end to end; only the default value and the reader that feeds it are missing. Not a naming mismatch, not a missing mechanism: an enforcement path that works, set to the wrong number with nothing able to change it. The value was deliberately chosen for parity when the page documented a default of 1 (v2.1.217-218); the page moved to 3 in v2.1.219 and we did not.

blastRadius: Crosses a WIRE boundary and a PERSISTENCE boundary — a risk trigger in this repo. `depth` rides the signed Pi execution manifest (`PiOrchestratorConfig`, harness-manifest.ts:31) from server-core to the pi-agent-server subprocess, and the derived `budgets.maxDepth` rides `PiChildStartInput` (`packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/child-session-port.ts:7-8`) and is persisted in the child-session record and session JSONL (see `packages/shared/src/sessions/__tests__/jsonl-permission-mode-normalization.test.ts:177`). Host-side revalidation is `packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/child-session-service.ts:574-576`, which rejects `depth > maxDepth` as 'child-session-budgets-invalid' — consistent after the change because the subprocess mints both from the same config. Readers of the value: spawner.ts:518 (refusal) and :602 (child budgets); SessionManager.ts:11141 (inherited.maxDepth on nested starts) and :4932 (plugin-hook path). Manifest-identity checks that must not be tripped: `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:1685-1689` pins the orchestrator the live subprocess was initialized with and fails `register_tools` with 'orchestrator mismatch' if a mid-session refresh shifts it — so the new value must come from a source that is stable for the session's lifetime (an env read at seed time is; a user-toggled setting would need the same generation discipline). `packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/pi-agent-init-contract.test.ts:207` asserts the literal source text `'maxDepth: config.orchestrator?.depth'` and will break if that line is reshaped. NOT affected: the pinned model-contract hashes — `piStaticModelContractPinKey` (harness-manifest.ts:312) branches only on `forkSubagent`, so raising depth cannot produce 'Pi execution manifest model contract mismatch'. Companion behaviour that changes what a user actually sees: the child tool pool. `packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/runtime-agent-definitions.ts:33-39` strips ORCHESTRATION_TOOLS (including `subagent`) from a tool-LESS imported descriptor's inherited ceiling (:140-:141), so raising the ceiling alone does not let a default imported agent nest; an agent that names `Agent`/`Task` explicitly resolves through `PI_RUNTIME_AGENT_TOOL_ALIASES` (`packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/runtime-agent-definition.ts:31`) and does get `subagent`, as does every fork (spawner.ts:332-353 inherits the session pool). Other suites that assert depth-1 budgets and should be swept: `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.child-partial-output.test.ts:22`, `SessionManager.auth-retry-lifecycle.test.ts:69`, `packages/pi-agent-server/src/harness/orchestrator-pin.test.ts:52`.
userImpact: Concrete and reachable today, on two surfaces. (1) A user installs a Claude plugin whose agent declares `tools` including `Agent` (a reviewer that fans out to verifiers is the doc's own example), the main session delegates to it, and that agent's first `subagent` call comes back `Subagent depth limit exceeded (1)`. The failed tool call shows only inside the subagent's own transcript; the main conversation just gets a thinner summary, so it reads as the agent choosing not to delegate rather than as a refusal. (2) With `NESSY_FORK_SUBAGENT=1`, a fork inherits the session's exact tool pool, so `subagent` is listed for it and returns the same error at the first nested call. Same for any `workflow` script running inside a subagent — every `agent()` call fails (workflow-tool.ts:605 passes the session depth). (3) An admin who copies Claude's documented `settings.json` env entry, in either spelling, gets no effect at all: nothing reads it, and there is no UI, setting or config file that raises the ceiling either — `orchestrator.depth` is documented in the pi-agent-server README as a knob but no host path populates it. What stays invisible: an imported agent that declares no `tools` never receives `subagent` in the first place (ORCHESTRATION_TOOLS strip), so for that shape the depth limit is latent behind an earlier one.
notes: Read every file cited. Three qualifications. (a) SCOPE — sub-agents.md:862 and :326 also bind the AT-LIMIT tool composition: at the ceiling the `Agent` tool must be withheld from a named subagent while a fork keeps it listed and gets an error. We implement the fork half correctly and, for named subagents, always return the call-time error instead of withholding the tool (spawner.ts:296 `allowedTools` has no depth input; spawner.ts:519-521's comment acknowledges this). That is a distinct divergence from the one filed here; raising the default from 1 to 3 does not create it but does make it reachable at layer 3 instead of layer 1. If it is folded into the same change, effort becomes L because the child tool pool is composed host-side and would need the child's depth. (b) The related session-wide caps `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION` (default 200) and `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS` (default 20) from env-vars.md:279 are separate findings and are also unimplemented; a plan that adds one env reader should probably add all three in the same module. (c) UNVERIFIED — I confirmed a managed-settings `env` block reaches process.env (`applyManagedEnv`, packages/shared/src/config/managed-delivery.ts:886) but did not trace whether a user-level settings `env` block does, which is the exact shape Claude's doc example at sub-agents.md:869-874 uses. If it does not, `NESSY_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` would be process-env-only and the doc's settings.json route would still not work.
